page: UpCloud GPU-24xCPU-480GB-2xH100 is an accelerator-focused instance designed for parallel computing, large-scale matrix operations, and artificial intelligence workloads. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor providing 24 physical x86_64 cores across 24 vCPUs operating at a 2.0 GHz base frequency. The architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), facilitating optimized hardware-level vector and integer math processing.

System memory totals 480 GB, establishing a high density of 20 GB of RAM per CPU core. Memory subsystems demonstrated high throughput in benchmark assessments, delivering 4,086.55 GB/s in cached small-block reads and 290.6 GB/s in large-block read transfers. The primary computational acceleration is supplied by two NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs providing a combined 160 GB of VRAM, targeted at high-capacity model parameters and parallel tensor calculations.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong parallel throughput. The system registered 10,457.59 tokens per second during small model prompt processing and 366.07 tokens per second during text generation. In CPU testing, the host recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 2,273.0, a multi-core score of 18,829.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 55,980.84. In-memory data throughput showed strength with 66.13 million operations per second during Redis SET tests.

The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address but contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for operating system persistence and dataset storage. Given the resource balance of 160 GB GPU memory and substantial host RAM, the instance is suited for large language model inference, distributed deep learning training, batch data processing, and scientific simulations.
